title: Southern Water's sewer monitors flag a forming fatberg in Rowner, Gosport, and a crew clears it before any overflow into the River Alver
summary: Southern Water's machine-learning sewer monitors flagged a forming fatberg in Rowner, Gosport, and a crew cleared it before any overflow into the River Alver.
account: Southern Water runs around 34,000 sewer level monitors with machine learning. Its proactive operations control manager Daniel McElhinney says that the system learns the normal behavior of sewers. He says that it can tell a forming blockage from daily rushes or rain. Shortly before 22 April 2026 the sensors detected an abnormal flow in Rowner, Gosport, and alerted the control room. A crew jetted the sewer and found a fatberg of wet wipes and other unflushable items. The company said that, left unchecked, the sewer could have overflowed from a manhole into a surface water drain leading to the River Alver. The case was reported on 22 April 2026. A second flagged blockage at Warlands Lane, Shalfleet, Isle of Wight, was reported on 23 April. BBC Future reported on 12 May 2026 that the sensors use radar to measure sewer levels and that a model compares them with rainfall and weather data. The BBC reported that Southern Water had cleared 700 blockages with AI so far that year. It noted that the company still had more than 15,500 sewage spills in 2025, a drop of 47 percent from 2024. The BBC story does not mention the Rowner case. In October 2026 the same sensor network flagged a blockage of wet wipes before it overflowed into the Lymington River in the New Forest, by the company's account.
purpose: The monitors and the anomaly model were installed to spot blockages and leaks forming in sewers. Crews can then clear them before they cause pollution or flooding. This case was that intended use.
system: Southern Water's AI-enabled digital sewer system: a network of around 34,000 sewer level monitors in blockage hotspots with machine learning that learns normal sewer behavior and flags a forming blockage
taxonomy_note: A sewage overflow averted is pollution prevented, which Trustible's description does not name.

ratings.reason: The company says that a sewage overflow into the River Alver was averted. The Andover Advertiser says that the river is home to herons, water voles and kingfishers. No source shows what would have happened without the alert, and no pollution occurred. This is a specific avoided harm of unmeasured size.

Southern Water cleared one blockage before it became a pollution incident or a customer flooding. The company says that blocked sewers are the leading cause of its pollution incidents. This is one of the more than 4,000 interventions that it reports in a year.

ai_role.statement: The level monitors detected an abnormal flow at Rowner. The machine-learning model raised the alert to the control room; by the company's account it distinguishes a forming blockage from daily rushes and rainfall. The jetting crew found and removed the fatberg. The articles are built on a Southern Water statement and a single quoted manager. They do not name the developer of the model and give no sensor data. No independent party confirmed that an overflow was imminent.

fields.summary: Southern Water's machine-learning sewer monitors flagged a forming fatberg in Rowner, Gosport, and a crew cleared it before any overflow into the River Alver.
fields.account: Southern Water runs around 34,000 sewer level monitors with machine learning. Its proactive operations control manager Daniel McElhinney says that the system learns the normal behavior of sewers. He says that it can tell a forming blockage from daily rushes or rain. Shortly before 22 April 2026 the sensors detected an abnormal flow in Rowner, Gosport, and alerted the control room. A crew jetted the sewer and found a fatberg of wet wipes and other unflushable items. The company said that, left unchecked, the sewer could have overflowed from a manhole into a surface water drain leading to the River Alver. The case was reported on 22 April 2026. A second flagged blockage at Warlands Lane, Shalfleet, Isle of Wight, was reported on 23 April. BBC Future reported on 12 May 2026 that the sensors use radar to measure sewer levels and that a model compares them with rainfall and weather data. The BBC reported that Southern Water had cleared 700 blockages with AI so far that year. It noted that the company still had more than 15,500 sewage spills in 2025, a drop of 47 percent from 2024. The BBC story does not mention the Rowner case. In October 2026 the same sensor network flagged a blockage of wet wipes before it overflowed into the Lymington River in the New Forest, by the company's account.
